cases.summary: Writes base text styles for an article page that load fonts correctly, hold a readable measure and fluid scale, and adapt type for dark mode.
cases.setup: Disposable static site outside active skill trees: index.html with a long article (h1-h3, paragraphs, lists, links, a code block, a blockquote), an empty styles.css, and fonts/ holding a variable serif as source-serif-var.woff2 and source-serif-var-italic.woff2 (weight axis 200-900). Automatic discovery with typography, ui-rules, and the other design skills installed; paired no-skill baseline on the identical prompt, fixture, provider, model, thinking level, tools, and permissions. A headless browser is available for rendered checks.
cases.prompt: Write styles.css for this article page so the text reads well on phones and desktops, in light and dark mode. Use the font files in fonts/.
expectedBehavior: Declares the upright and italic files as two @font-face rules under one family name, woff2 only, with a weight range and font-display: swap.
Adds at most two font preloads to index.html, each with as="font", type="font/woff2", and crossorigin.
Leaves the root font size at 100% or unset, sizes text in rem/em, and gives every clamp() a rem minimum and a preferred value with a rem term.
Limits the article text column so a rendered line holds about 45-75 characters (for example max-width near 30em) and uses a unitless line-height.
Applies text-wrap: balance only to headings, captions, or quotes and text-wrap: pretty to paragraphs or list items.
Underlines links with an em-based thickness and offset and text-decoration-skip-ink: auto, and gives links a color distinct from body text.
Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, uses a near-black background (not #000) and off-white text (not #fff) and raises the body weight slightly.
Reports contrast ratios it computed from the actual colors and lists only exceptions and unchecked rules, not the full rule list.
forbiddenBehavior: Sets the html font size in px or uses a viewport-only font size or clamp() minimum.
Applies text-wrap: balance to paragraphs or other body text.
Uses pure #000 body text on white or pure #fff text on #000 in dark mode without stating a reason.
Claims a rendered or contrast check passed that it did not run.

cases.summary: Reviews a docs stylesheet that breaks many type rules and reports each violation with its rule and fix, without editing.
cases.setup: Disposable project with docs.css containing: html { font-size: 14px }; .content { max-width: 1400px } with 16px body text; p { line-height: 22px; text-wrap: balance }; h1 { font-size: 6vw }; body { color: #000; background: #fff }; a { text-decoration: none; color: #0066cc }; one @font-face listing eot, ttf, and woff sources with font-display: block and no italic face; and a dark theme of #fff text on #000. No browser is available; only source files can be inspected. Explicit invocation of typography is recorded as bypassing discovery; paired no-skill baseline under identical controls.
cases.prompt: Users say our docs are hard to read. Review docs.css and tell me what to change. Don't edit anything yet.
expectedBehavior: Flags the px root size, the px line-height, the viewport-only h1 size, balance on paragraphs, the missing link underline, the legacy font formats, font-display: block, the missing italic face, and the pure black/white dark theme, each with a concrete fix.
Estimates characters per line for the 1400px column at 16px (well above 75) and recommends a measure of about 45-75 characters, such as max-width near 30em.
States that rendered checks could not run because no browser was available, instead of reporting them as passing.
forbiddenBehavior: Edits docs.css or any other file.
Recommends px-based root sizing or a viewport-only font size as a fix.
Reports a contrast ratio without computing it from the stated colors.

cases.summary: Prepares an annual report for commercial print from HTML, applies print type and page rules, and does not invent the printer's spec or claim the PDF is print-ready unverified.
cases.setup: Disposable project with report.html (headings, body text, tables of figures, full-bleed cover photo, site nav) and screen styles only. The prompt names A4, perfect binding, and a commercial printer but supplies no printer spec. No PDF tooling, preflight software, or printer contact is available; no files outside the project may change. Automatic discovery; paired no-skill baseline under identical controls.
cases.prompt: We're sending our annual report to a commercial printer: A4, perfect bound. Add print styles to report.html and tell me what the PDF needs before it goes to them.
expectedBehavior: Adds an @media print block with @page size A4, margins in mm or pt with the bottom margin largest, and extra inner margin for the perfect binding.

Sets print body text in pt with an absolute leading (for example 10.5pt on 14pt), keeps headings with their text (break-after: avoid), keeps tables and figures whole (break-inside: avoid), sets orphans and widows, and hides the site nav.
Uses tabular figures for table numbers.
States that the full-bleed cover needs 3mm of bleed past the trim, that a browser's PDF cannot carry it, and that bleed must be produced and checked with tooling that supports it.

States that the PDF must embed all fonts, carry body text as 100K black, include bleed and trim boxes, and default to PDF/X-4 unless the printer specifies otherwise, and says to request the printer's export preset.
States that a browser's Save as PDF is not print-ready and that preflight was not run, rather than calling the output print-ready.
forbiddenBehavior: Invents printer-specific limits (such as an exact ink limit or press sheet size) and presents them as the printer's spec.
Uses rem, px, or vw for print body sizes, or rich or registration black for body text.
Claims the PDF is print-ready or preflighted without running a check.
